cadence: weekly, Monday before the US open
method: Every Monday each open call is re-examined against the claims its note made. The numbers are computed from the record: where the call stands against what the note called for, how far the stop is, and a price-only range for where it can finish, drawn from the position's own recent volatility with no view assumed. The verdict is a judgment, stated with dated evidence: each claim the note relied on is re-measured and marked as holding or not, and the verdict has to follow from those marks. A broken thesis closes the call on the Scorecard from the review date. The return a note called for is written once and never changed.

latest.book_now: This review is three days late: Monday's scheduled run did not publish, so the record was re-measured on Thursday. After it the book is three calls, each with a physical constraint or a policy actor behind it: long US natural gas against war-priced oil, short wheat through the fund, and long the yen at the month-two retest of the July intervention. One call comes off. The long euro is closed because the reason behind it did not survive an honest re-test: over the full record since 2004, a stretched speculative euro short has more often been followed by a weaker euro than a stronger one, and the three-month gain the note quoted existed only inside a three-year window. Highest conviction: natural gas, which has earned twice what its note called for with the fund short still at a record, and wheat, where the fund selling the note predicted is now under way. Lowest: the yen, flat two and a half weeks in and waiting on the authorities. A reader holding the calls takes off the euro at today's close and leaves the other three alone.

book.basis: equal weight across the open calls, one unit each, trailing 63 sessions; a 21-session driftless range

book_risk.note: correlations are of daily mark changes over the trailing 63 sessions; exposure is the position's % move per 1% in equities or the dollar and per +10bp in the 10-year yield

calls.title: The most one-sided trade in the market is not on any chart
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate: median three-month euro return after speculative euro positioning at or below the 15th percentile (77% positive, 26 weeks)
calls.expected_basis: closed at the current mark of about -2.9%; with the edge disproven there is no expected recovery to add
calls.view_now: The reason for this call is gone. The gain the note quoted after a stretched speculative euro short exists only inside a three-year window; over the full record the same setup has lost money more often than it has made it. Meanwhile the dollar side has run against us as the note's own risk described, with US yields higher and the euro near a 17-month low. We no longer expect this call to reach what the note called for.
calls.action_reason: A broken thesis is closed whatever the price has done. The evidence the call rested on did not hold up on the full record, so it comes off now rather than running to its November horizon or its stop.

driver_checks.now: re-tested on the full record since 2004 with each week ranked only against the history available that week: nine separate episodes, an average loss of 1.2% over three months, one in three won; the speculators were more often right
driver_checks.source: MacroTilt outside-research challenge re-test of the euro positioning signal (CFTC record 2004 to 2026)

calls.title: The last buyers just showed up in wheat
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate between its one-month (−5.3%) and three-month (−6.6%) medians for a two-month horizon, taken as a short return
calls.expected_basis: the current mark of about +3.8% plus roughly a point and a half more, a little under the base rate because funds have already sold out of their length and there is less selling left to come
calls.view_now: The unwind the note called for is happening: funds that were record long when the call was made are now net short, and wheat has fallen from 716 at entry to 686. The fund the reader shorts is down about 4% as of Tuesday's mark, most of what the note called for, with four weeks left. Much of the selling is now done, so the remaining edge is smaller than at entry, but nothing argues against the call.
calls.action_reason: Driver intact and working as described, stop far away. It runs to its early-November horizon.

calls.title: Oil carries a war premium. US natural gas carries none.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate: median front-month gas gain over three months after an oil-to-gas ratio reading at or above the 95th percentile (42 episodes since 2004)
calls.expected_basis: the current mark of about +15.4% with no further drift added, because the ratio has fallen back below the extreme the base rate was measured from; the record fund short is a risk to the upside, not a number we add
calls.view_now: This has done what the base rate said an extreme of this kind does, and more: gas is up 15% against the 7.6% the note called for, four weeks into a thirteen-week horizon, while oil has given back its premium. The ratio is no longer extreme, so the edge that set up the call is largely spent; what remains is a record fund short in gas that would have to be bought back. We expect the call to finish roughly where it is now, with a wide range either side.
calls.action_reason: Driver intact and the stop is a third away. It runs to its December horizon; with the edge mostly earned, the review will close it early if the ratio swings back toward oil or the fund short is bought back.

calls.title: The record yen rescue looks dead. So did the last three at exactly this point.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's target: 147 on dollar-yen by late January 2027, the median months-two-to-six move applied from 157.34, roughly +6% on the fund
calls.expected_basis: the note's base rate unchanged: the median months-two-to-six move in dollar-yen after an intervention campaign (−6.9%), roughly +6% on the fund before costs, with the position where it entered
calls.view_now: Two and a half weeks in and flat, which is what month two looked like in the prior campaigns. The authorities repeated their readiness to act alongside the US at the end of September and the yen did not weaken through the jobs report. Nothing has been tested yet; three prior episodes is a thin record, as the note said, and one counterexample would change the median.
calls.action_reason: Nothing has changed since publication; the call is under three weeks into a four-month horizon with the driver in place.
